thesis: XLK holds NVIDIA at roughly 16% and about 45% of the fund in its top five, so for this book it is not diversification - it is NVDA, MSFT and AMD again, wrapped in a fee. We already own all three directly. Add the weakest seasonal month on record for this ETF and a hike now priced at 62.2%, and there is nothing to buy here.
bull_case: The trend is intact - close > SMA50 > SMA200 with 63d momentum +5.0% and RSI 54 - and ATR of 1.6% makes it cheap to hold. The valuation case is not silly: three of the top five holdings, about 45% of the fund, have been trading at historically low P/E multiples, with NVIDIA at roughly 23x its current-year outlook. Sell-side work argues XLK is in rebound mode and could advance 25% over twelve months as AI results keep driving the leaders. The underlying earnings support it: Azure guided +44-45% cc, Nvidia guided $108B.
bear_case: The overlap is the whole objection. XLK's largest holding is NVDA at ~16%, and we own NVDA, MSFT and AMD outright; buying XLK quadruples down on one factor while calling it a sector allocation. Seasonality is against it specifically: September has the lowest probability of a positive return of any month for this ETF at 46.15%, against 81.82% for November. The central 2026 risk is the return on AI capex - the same question hanging over every position in the book - and worries about AI spending sustainability have been weighing on the sector. Macro turned hawkish again today: CME FedWatch has the odds of a hike next week back to 62.2%, up from roughly 49-51% yesterday, with PPI out today and August CPI tomorrow morning as the last inflation reads before the 15-16 Sep FOMC. Brent is $101.25 after US forces destroyed five Iranian tankers and Houthi strikes hit Saudi energy facilities.
catalysts: August CPI on 11 Sep and the 15-16 Sep FOMC
Q3 earnings from the megacap holdings in late Oct
risks: ~16% NVDA and ~45% top-five concentration duplicating positions we already hold
September is XLK's weakest month at 46.15% positive
AI capex ROI is the sector's central unresolved question
Rate shock with hike odds back at 62.2%
invalidation: Flips long on a weekly close above 195 made after the 16 Sep FOMC - strength through the event rather than into it. The bear case confirms on a close below 178, which breaks the SMA50 and the summer range.
